summary: Independent DAY discovery pass covered all 12 Chief-selected active-batch companies and refreshed several decision-relevant weak signals. Fresh primary/company evidence strengthens demand signals for RKLB, NVDA, AVGO, TSM, ARM, ANET and VRT, but none closes T0 methodology gaps by itself. Universe-wide discovery remains fail-closed because the cadence-due active gating discovery families were not all independently cleared in this lane and FINRA remains partition-freshness only with eventDataAvailable=false. A separate source-integrity defect was detected in the discovery pool: three literal FILE CREATION TIME footer strings were ingested as outside-universe tickers and should be quarantined by the owning lane/Chief rather than treated as discoveries.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: Electron completed its 16th launch of 2026 on September 11 and Q2 reported record revenue/backlog plus Neutron first-flight hardware milestones; this is a real operating-cadence signal, not proof of Neutron economics.
contradictions: Launch cadence is de-risking Electron operations while Neutron schedule/capital intensity and acquisition integration remain unresolved.
unknowns: Neutron qualification schedule, cancellation quality of backlog, acquisition funding bridge.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Electron cadence or Neutron hardware milestones materially reverse, or backlog fails to convert without compensating economics.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: September 1 results filing is fresh and September insider ownership activity is visible, but the signal does not resolve hyperscaler/end-customer durability or insourcing risk.
contradictions: Strong operating momentum coexists with concentration risk already identified in the queue.
unknowns: True end-customer program duration, insourcing probability, acquisition cash bridge.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: A major customer program rolls off or insources connectivity faster than replacement demand emerges.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: No newly verified regulatory/procurement signal in this pass changes the active thesis; recent ownership filings do not close end-customer mapping or warrant-vesting questions.
contradictions: Strong platform narrative remains ahead of independently normalized customer concentration evidence.
unknowns: End-customer mapping, refreshed control ownership, future customer-warrant vesting.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Key platform design wins are delayed/lost or dilution/control economics prove materially worse than current assumptions.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: AWS announced deployment of 2 million additional NVIDIA GPUs across 2027-2028 plus deeper CPU/networking/robotics integration; this independently strengthens platform breadth while the 10-Q keeps export-control sensitivity explicit.
contradictions: Demand acceleration and deeper platform attachment coexist with policy-driven addressable-market loss and customer concentration.
unknowns: Long-run wallet share versus custom accelerators, breadth of future export controls, normalized customer concentration.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Major hyperscalers shift incremental AI capex materially toward internal/custom silicon without offsetting NVIDIA platform growth.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: Q2 revenue reached $11.5B and data-center revenue $6.7B, up 107% year over year, while named Helios/Instinct deployment partners broaden the observable customer set.
contradictions: Rapid deployment growth does not yet establish durable accelerator margins or share against NVIDIA/custom silicon.
unknowns: Instinct customer concentration, repeat-deployment economics, export-license sensitivity.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Named deployments fail to convert into repeat scaled orders or accelerator economics remain structurally inferior.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: Q3 revenue was $29.6B, AI semiconductor revenue $16.7B and Q4 AI semiconductor guidance $21.7B, reinforcing exceptional custom-accelerator/networking demand.
contradictions: Acceleration strengthens the bottleneck thesis while making a few very large AI programs even more decision-relevant.
unknowns: AI customer concentration by program, refinancing path, VMware tax-indemnity tail risk.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: One or more anchor custom-accelerator programs migrate away or expected AI revenue acceleration fails without a broad replacement base.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: August consolidated revenue was NT$514.806B, up 53.3% year over year; the monthly series now shows 39.3% year-to-date growth through August.
contradictions: Demand remains very strong while Taiwan concentration and overseas-fab cost normalization remain unaddressed by topline momentum.
unknowns: Customer concentration, overseas-fab margin drag, geopolitical resilience premium.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Advanced-node demand or yields materially weaken, or overseas redundancy destroys more economics than pricing can offset.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: Q2 net sales were EUR9.3B with EUR11-12B Q3 guidance and EUR43-45B 2026 sales guidance, preserving strong lithography demand visibility.
contradictions: Demand/backlog visibility remains strong while China/export mix and High-NA utilization are policy/customer-dependent.
unknowns: Current China mix, critical-supplier concentration, customer High-NA ROI.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Broad order deferrals or expanding controls materially reduce service/system economics while High-NA adoption lags.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: Q1 FYE27 revenue rose 22% to $1.289B; data-center royalties more than doubled and disclosed AGI CPU demand across FYE27-28 now exceeds $2B, with initial product delivered to multiple customers.
contradictions: Platform expansion into production silicon increases opportunity but also execution/capacity/capital complexity relative to pure IP economics.
unknowns: Related-party economics, SoftBank/control governance, customer concentration, AGI CPU margin/capacity economics.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: AGI CPU demand fails to convert at acceptable margins or major licensees shift meaningful workloads to alternatives.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: HBM4 is in high-volume shipment for the lead customer and samples are with multiple end-customers; September 30 earnings is the next high-information event.
contradictions: HBM scarcity and exceptional profitability may be durable structurally or may attract enough supply to recreate memory-cycle mean reversion.
unknowns: Competitor HBM4 yields/capacity, contract floors, normalized capex/debt through the cycle.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: HBM share/yield leadership erodes or supply expansion causes rapid ASP/margin compression.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: Q2 revenue exceeded $3B, up 37.7% year over year, alongside 1.6Tbps AI-fabric products and 60% lower interconnect power claims for linear pluggable optics.
contradictions: Strong innovation and growth do not independently resolve cloud-titan concentration or proprietary-fabric substitution.
unknowns: Current top-customer shares, buyer breadth for 1.6T, white-box/custom-network displacement risk.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Large cloud customers internalize material networking share or Arista loses major AI-fabric designs.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: September 2 agreement to acquire UtilityInnovation Group for ~$1.45B cash plus up to $1.15B contingent consideration extends Vertiv from power/cooling toward microgrid orchestration and behind-the-meter power, a meaningful constraint-migration signal.
contradictions: The acquisition increases strategic coverage of time-to-power while adding integration, valuation and execution risk.
unknowns: Customer concentration, backlog cancellation/reschedule quality, UIG integration economics and contingent-payment probability.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Behind-the-meter demand fails to convert or acquisition integration dilutes returns while core backlog conversion weakens.

materialFindings.finding: NVDA/AWS expansion, AVGO Q3 acceleration, TSM August revenue, ARM AGI CPU demand and ANET Q2 growth all independently confirm that AI infrastructure demand remains unusually strong across multiple stack layers, but these signals are correlated to the same capex regime and must not be counted as independent macro proof.

VRT's UtilityInnovation Group acquisition is a credible new signal that the data-center constraint is migrating from rack power/cooling toward time-to-power, microgrid controls and behind-the-meter generation orchestration.

The discovery pool currently contains literal exchange-file footer strings as tickers (FILE CREATION TIME...), indicating parser contamination that must not be treated as genuine newly listed securities.
BURU was detected as a newly listed/outside-universe symbol by the official directory and requires business-relevance/identity screening before any admission consideration.

contradictions: Machine discovery reports healthy required-source reachability, but FINRA is still partition-freshness only and row-level corporate-action event data is unavailable without a bearer token.
Strong multi-company AI demand signals are correlated to one capex regime and should not be counted as independent macro confirmations.
Discovery-pool FILE CREATION TIME entries conflict with entity semantics and appear to be parser artifacts rather than securities.
unknowns: All cadence-due active gating discovery families have not been independently cleared in this lane for 20260914T1200Z.
BURU business relevance and corporate identity have not been fully screened.
No sensor-only finding in this pass is promoted to canonical score/rank influence.

accuracyDebates.reason: Malformed discovery entities can create false challengers and contaminate outside-universe screening.
Multiple AI-stack companies can all reflect one underlying hyperscaler capex event; counting them as independent macro evidence inflates confidence.
VRT's UIG deal provides a concrete primary-source signal that behind-the-meter orchestration may be becoming a distinct bottleneck worth structural review.
